When both factors are whole numbers, then:

$\blueE{\text{factor}} \times \blueE{\text{factor}} = \maroonD{\text{multiple}}$

###Multiples of $8$

$\begin{align}
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{1} &= \maroonD{8}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{2} &= \maroonD{16}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{3} &= \maroonD{24}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{4} &= \maroonD{32}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{5} &= \maroonD{40}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{6} &= \maroonD{48}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{7} &= \maroonD{56}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{8} &= \maroonD{64}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{9} &= \maroonD{72}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{10} &= \maroonD{80}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{11} &= \maroonD{88}\\\\
\blueE{8} \times \blueE{12} &= \maroonD{96}
\end{align}$

All of the shaded numbers in the table are multiples of $\blueE{8}$. Every multiple of $8$ between $1$ and $100$ is shaded.
The shaded numbers on the hundred chart are only the multiples of $8$.
